info.name: Raj-PG API
info.description: Generated from backend/src by backend/scripts/generate-postman.mjs; regenerate with `npm run postman` in backend/. Start with Auth: sign in, then run any request. See api/README.md.

request.description:
One form for both user types: the account type is discovered from the credentials rather than chosen up front. Super admins are checked first; they only have emails, so a phone number goes straight to the resident check. The response matches GET /auth/session.

Source: backend/src/auth.ts

The signed-in super admin edits their own account. A name change needs nothing more; changing the sign-in email or password needs the current password, so an unattended session cannot be used to take the account over. Other sessions are signed out when the password changes. Identity details are all-or-nothing: the Settings form always sends them (and must fill them all), while a body that omits them leaves the stored ones untouched.

Source: backend/src/auth.ts

Lets the web app decide which experience to render without knowing the user type up front.

Accepts the policy version the resident was shown. If the owner changed a policy again since, the versions differ and the resident is sent back to read the newer text.

Source: backend/src/residentPortal.ts

"I've paid" after sending rent to the owner's UPI ID. The server, not the browser, decides the amount and months (rentItemsToPay: what is owed, else next month in advance); with no rent set up it takes the amount the resident typed, with no months. The owner confirms it against their bank app. One open report at a time, so a double tap cannot file two.

Source: backend/src/residentPortal.ts

Shows a UPI QR for everything owed. The amount is snapshotted into a RentOrder keyed by the QR id, plus a pending Payment so the owner's Payments list shows it; an open code for the same amount is reused, so refreshing the page does not pile up pending rows.

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

The owner's decision on a resident's identity documents (Aadhaar, or passport and visa). Approval needs every detail and the upload on file, because that is what the owner attests to having checked.

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

The key is only stored hashed, so "editing" it means issuing a new one. This is also the forgotten-password path: the resident's password is cleared so the new key works for sign-in. With { send: true } the new key is also sent to the resident by email and WhatsApp.

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

A super admin's decision on a resident a receptionist added: approve lets them sign in; reject removes them and frees the room, since they never became a resident. Super admins only (see staffGuard.ts).

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

Cancels a concession before its month is paid (once paid, the discount is already in the record).

Source: backend/src/referrals.ts

Approve (close the account now) or decline with a reason (the request is cleared, the account carries on, and the resident sees the reason). Dues do not block approval: the owner sees them and decides.

Source: backend/src/accountDeletion.ts

Lets the owner choose a resident's password so they can tell the resident what it is; the password itself is stored only as a hash. Retires the access key and signs the resident out. Door lock PIN: POST issues a new one (replacing any old one, which the owner then reprograms), DELETE removes it. Super admins only (see staffGuard). Anyone who has left gets no key. Each change also queues the matching PIN change for the owner to make on the lock (see doorLockTasks.ts).

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

Completes an approved move-out on or after its date: the resident becomes inactive and is signed out, gives up the room (free for the next resident at once), and keeps their record and rent history, with movedOutFrom noting where they lived.

Source: backend/src/exits.ts

Approve or decline a pending request; the resident is emailed either way.

Source: backend/src/exits.ts

Declines a resident's request to join the food plan; approving is a normal update with foodOpted: true.

Source: backend/src/residents.ts

Deletes a record on the Deleted records page for good. Only closed accounts: a live resident is removed (and kept) first, so one click can never erase someone. Super admins only (see staffGuard.ts).
